nodes.summary: Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be finite and $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. The interpolation polynomial $f_X \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ of $f$ on $X$ has degree less than $|X|$, where the zero polynomial has degree $-\infty$.

nodes.summary: Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be finite and $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. The interpolation polynomial $f_X \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ of $f$ on $X$ satisfies $f_X(x) = f(x)$ for every $x \in X$.

nodes.title: Exchange formula for interpolation polynomials

nodes.summary: Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be finite and $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. The interpolation polynomial $f_X \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ of $f$ on $X$ is the Lagrange interpolation polynomial: the unique polynomial with rational coefficients of degree less than $|X|$ such that $f_X(x) = f(x)$ for every $x \in X$.
nodes.title: Interpolation polynomial

nodes.summary: Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, and write $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ for the ring of locally integer polynomial functions on $U$: the functions $U \to \mathbb{Z}$ whose restriction to every finite subset of $U$ agrees with a polynomial with integer coefficients. Let $f \in \mathrm{LIP}(U)$. If $|f(x)|$ is a prime number for infinitely many $x \in U$, then $f$ is irreducible in the ring $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$.
nodes.title: LIP functions with infinitely many prime values are irreducible

nodes.summary: Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ and let $f : U \to \mathbb{Z}$ lie in the ring $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ of locally integer polynomial functions on $U$. If $f(x) = 0$ for infinitely many $x \in U$, then $f(x) = 0$ for every $x \in U$.
nodes.title: A locally integer polynomial function with infinitely many zeros is zero

nodes.summary: Let $U \subseteq V \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ with $U$ infinite, and let $f, g : V \to \mathbb{Z}$ lie in the ring $\mathrm{LIP}(V)$ of locally integer polynomial functions on $V$. If $f(x) = g(x)$ for every $x \in U$, then $f = g$.
nodes.title: Locally integer polynomial functions agreeing on an infinite subset are equal

nodes.summary: Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ have finite complement, let $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$, and for $S \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ write $\mathrm{LIP}(S)$ for the ring of locally integer polynomial (LIP) functions $S \to \mathbb{Z}$. Then the restriction of $f$ to $U$ lies in $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ if and only if every $a \in U$ lies in some $W \subseteq U$ with…
nodes.title: Locally integer polynomial functions on cofinite sets of primes

Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ have density one and let $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. Then the restriction of $f$ to $U$ lies in $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ if and only if every…

Let $U$ be a set of positive integers of natural density one and let $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. Then the restriction of $f$ to $U$ lies in $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ if and…
nodes.title: Locally integer polynomial functions on density one sets of positive integers

nodes.summary: For every infinite $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, the ring $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ of locally integer polynomial functions $U \to \mathbb{Z}$ is an integral domain.
nodes.title: Locally integer polynomial functions on an infinite set form a domain

nodes.summary: Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, let $\mathbb{N} = \{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$, and let $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to U$ be a bijection. For a sequence of integers $a = (a_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ define $f_a : U \to \mathbb{Z}$ by
nodes.title: Newton series of locally integer polynomial functions

nodes.summary: For every infinite set $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, the only units of the ring $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ of locally integer polynomial functions on $U$ are the constant functions $1$ and $-1$.
nodes.title: Units of $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$

nodes.summary: For $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ is the subring of the ring of all functions $U \to \mathbb{Z}$ (with pointwise operations) consisting of the functions $f$ such that for every finite subset $X \subseteq U$ there is a polynomial $p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $p(x) = f(x)$ for all $x \in X$.
nodes.title: The ring $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ of locally integer polynomial functions

nodes.summary: Let $a_1, a_2 \ge 0$ and $d_1, d_2 \ge 1$ be integers, let $U_i = \{a_i + d_i n : n \in \mathbb{Z}, n \ge 0\}$ for $i = 1, 2$, and suppose $U_1 \cap U_2$ is nonempty. If $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ restricts to an element of $\mathrm{LIP}(U_1)$ on $U_1$ and to an element of $\mathrm{LIP}(U_2)$ on $U_2$, then the restriction of $f$ to $U_1 \cup U_2$ lies in $\mathrm{LIP}(U_1 \cup U_2)$.
nodes.title: Gluing LIP functions on two intersecting progressions

nodes.summary: If $f$ and $g$ lie in $\mathrm{LIP}(\mathbb{Z})$, the ring of locally integer polynomial functions $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$, then so does the composite $x \mapsto f(g(x))$.
nodes.title: $\mathrm{LIP}(\mathbb{Z})$ is closed under composition

nodes.summary: If $f$ lies in $\mathrm{LIP}(\mathbb{Z})$, the ring of locally integer polynomial functions $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$, then so does the function $x \mapsto f(x) - f(x - 1)$.
nodes.title: $\mathrm{LIP}(\mathbb{Z})$ is closed under the discrete derivative

nodes.summary: Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be finite, let $q \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ have degree less than $|X|$, and let $p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ satisfy $q(x) = p(x)$ for all $x \in X$. Then $q$ has integer coefficients, that is, $q$ is the image in $\mathbb{Q}[x]$ of a polynomial in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.
nodes.title: Integrality of low-degree interpolants

nodes.summary: For $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ and $f : U \to \mathbb{Z}$, $f$ lies in $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ if and only if for every finite subset $X \subseteq U$ there is a polynomial $p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $p(x) = f(x)$ for all $x \in X$.
nodes.title: Membership in $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$

nodes.summary: Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, let $C$ be a real number and $d \ge 0$ an integer, and let $f \in \mathrm{LIP}(U)$. If $|f(x)| \le C|x|^d$ for infinitely many $x \in U$, then there is a polynomial $p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $f(x) = p(x)$ for all $x \in U$.
nodes.title: A LIP function bounded by $C|x|^d$ infinitely often is a polynomial

nodes.summary: Let $f$ lie in $\mathrm{LIP}(\mathbb{Z})$, the ring of locally integer polynomial functions $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. If $|f(x)| < (2|x| - 1)!/2^{2|x| - 1}$ for all but finitely many $x \in \mathbb{Z}$, then there is a polynomial $p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $f(x) = p(x)$ for all $x \in \mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.title: LIP functions on $\mathbb{Z}$ below the factorial bound are polynomials

nodes.summary: Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be infinite, and map each $p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ to the function $u \mapsto p(u)$ in $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$. Let $f \in \mathrm{LIP}(U)$ and let $Q$ be a nonzero polynomial with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ such that $Q(f) = 0$ in $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$, where the coefficients of $Q$ are mapped into $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ in this way. Then there is $p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $f(u) = p(u)$ for all…
nodes.title: $\mathbb{Z}(x)$ is algebraically closed in $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$

nodes.summary: Let $a_1, a_2, d_1, d_2, a, b$ be natural numbers with $d_1, d_2 > 0$, where $\mathbb{N} = \{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$, and let $P_i = \{a_i + d_i n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ for $i = 1, 2$. If $a \in P_1$, $b \in P_2$, $P_1 \cap P_2$ is nonempty and $a \neq b$, then $P_1 \cap P_2$ contains infinitely many elements of the progression $\{\min(a, b) + |a - b|\, n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$.
nodes.title: Two intersecting progressions share infinitely many terms with a third

nodes.summary: Let $a_1, a_2, d_1, d_2$ be natural numbers with $d_1, d_2 > 0$, where $\mathbb{N} = \{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$, and let $P_i = \{a_i + d_i n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ for $i = 1, 2$. Then $P_1 \cap P_2$ is nonempty if and only if $\gcd(d_1, d_2)$ divides the integer $a_1 - a_2$, and if $P_1 \cap P_2$ is nonempty, then $P_1 \cap P_2 = \{a_3 + \operatorname{lcm}(d_1, d_2)\, n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ for some $a_3 \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Intersection of two arithmetic progressions of natural numbers

nodes.summary: For $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, an integer polynomial $p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ and $u \in U$, the image of $p$ under the evaluation map $\mathbb{Z}[x] \to \mathrm{LIP}(U)$ takes the value $p(u)$ at $u$.
nodes.title: Values of the evaluation map into LIP(U)

nodes.summary: For every infinite set $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, the evaluation map $\mathbb{Z}[x] \to \mathrm{LIP}(U)$, sending $p$ to the function $u \mapsto p(u)$, is injective: distinct integer polynomials give distinct functions on $U$.
nodes.title: Integer polynomials embed in LIP(U)

nodes.summary: For $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, the evaluation map is the ring homomorphism from $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ to the ring $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ of locally integer polynomial functions on $U$ that sends each integer polynomial $p$ to the function $U \to \mathbb{Z}$, $u \mapsto p(u)$.
nodes.title: The evaluation map from $\mathbb{Z}(x)$ to $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$

nodes.summary: Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be infinite and let $p$ be a prime element of $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ (a prime of $\mathbb{Z}$, or an irreducible integer polynomial of content $1$). Then the function $u \mapsto p(u)$, the image of $p$ under the evaluation map $\mathbb{Z}[x] \to \mathrm{LIP}(U)$, is a prime element of $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$.
nodes.title: Prime integer polynomials stay prime in LIP(U)

nodes.summary: The function $x \mapsto x(x+1)/2$ on $\mathbb{Z}$ (an integer, since $x(x+1)$ is even) does not belong to $\mathrm{LIP}(\mathbb{Z})$: no integer polynomial $p$ takes the values $0, 0, 1$ at $-1, 0, 1$, since $1 - (-1)$ must divide $p(1) - p(-1)$.
nodes.title: The triangular-number function is not LIP on the integers

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
